- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion or downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or use lagged mean as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (0.00) and prices are trending down, model underestimates — adjust downward by 2–5% of recent range to capture bearish continuation.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed — add 1–3% buffer to forecast for volatility amplification.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0,1,0,1), model exhibits lagged reaction — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to match sentiment momentum.
- In cases where true outcome diverges >10% from 30d forecast mean, check if sentiment was absent in last 5 days — if so, apply “sentiment lag penalty” by reducing forecast by 3–5% to account for delayed reaction.
